Measured concentration: '=' is 22.82% of final reset tokens versus 11.00% of continued tokens. In 64 reset outputs versus 25 continued outputs, at least half the tokens are '='.
Example versus aggregate: prompt 0 has entropy 3.060 for reset versus 2.050 for continued. That one passage reverses the pooled ranking; the graph counts all 256 outputs.

Formatting sensitivity: excluding '=' shrinks the entropy gap from 0.620 to 0.122 nats. Repeated-four-gram rates on retained original windows become 44.61% versus 45.22% (reset/continued), with different retained counts.

Interpretation: real-text prediction and generated-token concentration are different behaviours. Reset preserves better real-test scores while emitting more heading loops. The symbol concentration is measured; why the training policy favours those loops is untested.
Scope: six adjacent articles supply this probe; 79.39% of its prompt tokens come from the first three. These are descriptive diagnostics, not full-corpus diversity or evidence of semantic quality.

items.text: A: '=' frequency. B: raw entropy (solid), excluding '=' (dashed). C: individual-output entropy. D: matched final prompts; pink marks the quoted passage. All panels use the fixed 256-prompt probe.

Intuition: one answer can repeat Nintendo while other answers repeat different words. Pooling all their tokens can still give a broad mix. The graph and an individual passage answer different questions.
The quoted passage: continued is more repetitive here. Its entropy is 2.050 nats versus reset's 3.060; its internal repeated-four-gram rate is 68.85% versus 36.07%.

The measured overall driver: '=' takes 22.82% of reset tokens versus 11.00% of continued tokens. Reset has 64 outputs with at least 32 '=' tokens; continued has 25. These are actual generated symbols.
Pooling can conceal loops: continued pooled entropy stays near S0, while mean entropy within an output falls 2.966 to 2.708. Different passages can repeat different tokens.
Sensitivity check: excluding '=' shrinks the entropy gap 0.620 to 0.122 nats. Frequencies are renormalized over 12,645 versus 14,581 remaining tokens; this does not replace the primary metric.

What this means: formatting strongly affects raw-token diversity. It does not measure semantic knowledge. The probe covers six adjacent articles; why reset produces more heading loops remains unresolved.
